Key asks from the acct: keep P95 latency < 700ms and reduce per-token unit cost where we can without impacting output quality.

Attachments: acme_warm_launch_MVP_intake.docx, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

- Monica: lead success & timeline, run the kickoff workshop and own the MAP milestones.
- Marissa: coordinate implementation deliverables and timeline with Acme’s SRE.
- Karthik: technical recommendations for batching, KV/cache strategy, and quant profile suggestions for an initial canary.

I’ve added procurement on cc because they’ll need the DocuSign once we lock the reserved capacity for the first month. I’ll host a 30-min alignment tomorrow 10am PT — please confirm availability.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Warm-launch handoff: cost & perf tuning plan for Acme AI

Thanks — reviewed the intake and sample responses. High-level recommendations for canary (5% traffic):

1) Batching
- Use adaptive batching with a 18–25ms batch window initially. For this workload (median 280 tokens), that window yields good utilization without spiking latency.
- Configure a max batch size of 32 for generation requests; allow smaller batches for shorter prompts.

2) KV / Prefix Caching
- Enable prefix KV caching on routes that are expected to repeat (heuristic: >10% repeated prefix within 1h). Set KV TTL to 30m to balance freshness and hit rate.
- We’ll instrument cache hit-rate and token-savings in the metrics dashboard.

3) Quantization Profiles
- Suggest starting with the conservative-int8 profile (q8) for the canary to reduce cost ~25% vs FP16 with minimal quality delta on their prompt set. If token-level quality checks look stable, evaluate nf4/int4 on a secondary rollout.
- Attachments: quick mapping of profiles -> expected cost delta and ops risk.

4) Routing & Fallbacks
- Route 95% of traffic to the dedicated pool and 5% to canary. Have automatic fallback to smaller but compatible model variant in the same region if latency breaches >850ms for 2 consecutive mins.

5) Metrics / Acceptance
- Track: P95 latency, tokens per request, cache hit-rate, generation rejection/errors, and a prompt-set quality score we’ll compute via eval harness daily.
- Create dashboard panels and add alert for P95 > 800ms.

I’ll produce a short runbook for the workshop describing how to flip quant profiles and routing percentages safely (will attach tomorrow). If Marissa can coordinate a test user with Acme SRE, we can do a controlled traffic replay on Friday.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
